clue.text: Money Miss Borden got for old car

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
Lizzie Borden, the notorious American accused of the 1892 axe murders

explanation.surface: A woman named Borden was paid for an elderly motor.
explanation.walkthrough: TIN LIZZIE was the nickname of the Ford Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname belonged to Ford's Model T, a cheap early motor vehicle now long obsolete.

clue.text: Riot over receiving head of Danish royal house

indicators.note: the turned word takes in a letter
in a down clue over means the word is turned upward

parts.note: a rout is an old word for a riot or disorderly crowd

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of Danish

explanation.surface: Disorder after a Danish chief is taken in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns ROUT into TUOR; D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors ruled England from 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: She, for example, gets yen after short time for something original

indicators.note: after here means placed behind in the word, so the currency letter comes at the end following the time letter

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
T is short for time
Y is the symbol for yen

explanation.surface: A woman receives Japanese money after a brief spell, which is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' looks like a pronoun; it is Haggard's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelty is a new or unusual thing.

clue.text: Shot on state thoroughfare furthest from border

parts.note: an inner is a shot hitting the ring just outside the bull on a target
MO is the abbreviation for Missouri
ST is short for street

explanation.surface: Someone shot dead on a state highway far from the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like an anagram signal; it is a shot at a target.
explanation.definitionFit: Innermost means most deeply inside, so furthest from the edge.

clue.text: Is a razor not unusual for Parsee?

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are set in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A man of an Indian faith asks whether owning a razor is odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsees are Indian followers of the Persian prophet Zoroaster.

clue.text: Decline of Mrs Browning, initially

indicators.note: initially here means taking the initials of the poet's full name, the first letter of each part

parts.note: the Victorian poet Elizabeth Barrett Browning
her maiden surname, Barrett, kept in her full name
her married surname, from the poet Robert Browning

explanation.surface: Elizabeth Barrett Browning's early fall in fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet signed herself by her three initials; 'initially' asks for the first letter of each of her names.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling away, like a tide going out, is what this word means.

clue.text: Choose one council leader of vision

parts.note: to opt is to choose
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of council

explanation.surface: Pick a single local-government head who has foresight.
explanation.definitionFit: Optic is an adjective relating to the eye and sight.

clue.text: Plant that's source of meat sauce

parts.note: the ox gives beef
sauce and lip both mean cheek, impudence

explanation.surface: A vegetable that is the base of a meat gravy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' looks culinary; it means cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxlip is a wild flowering herb related to the primrose.

clue.text: Toil frantically to secure rent in Mediterranean port

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the other piece inside
frantic work scrambles the letters of toil

parts.note: a rent is a tear or rip

explanation.surface: Hard work to pay the rent in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' makes TOLI from TOIL; 'rent' looks like payment but is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli, capital of Libya, is a port on the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Something that beats flattery as a sweetener?

parts.note: a cane is used to beat someone
sugar can mean sweet talk, flattery

explanation.surface: Something better than flattery for winning people round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beats' suggests surpassing; it means striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar from cane is a common sweetening agent, the question mark marking definition by example.

clue.text: Rod has a dip when he discovers water

definitions.text: Rod has a dip when he discovers water

parts.words: Rod has a dip when he discovers water
parts.note: a dowser's rod dips when the person holding it finds underground water, so the clue describes such a water-finder

explanation.surface: A man called Rod goes for a swim when he finds water.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name taking a swim; it is the dowsing rod, which twitches downward over hidden water.
explanation.definitionFit: A water dowser locates underground springs with a forked rod that dips over them.

clue.text: Ring accepted by speculator in gold, perhaps

parts.note: a bull is a stock-market speculator betting on rising prices

indicators.note: the ring is taken into the speculator and the following word, sitting inside them

parts.note: taken as written
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A wedding ring taken on by a market trader dealing in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion is precious metal in bars or ingots, gold being the usual example.

clue.text: Some were lured back for a sovereign

indicators.note: back tells us the run is read in the opposite direction
only some of the letters of the words were lured are used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: Some people were tempted back by a gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sovereign' looks like the coin; it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign is a monarch, someone who governs a realm.

clue.text: Vague change accepted by husband in loving environment

indicators.note: loving forms an environment, surrounding the other letters

parts.note: amorous means loving
P, for pence, is small change
H, the standard abbreviation for husband, which takes on the change just ahead of it

explanation.surface: A husband warmly agrees to an unclear alteration in a romantic setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' looks like the definition's partner in alteration; it is small change, the penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amorphous has no definite shape, so it is ill-defined.

clue.text: Form of aid the poor originally claimed for such treatment

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective describing this treatment

indicators.note: a form of the words is a new arrangement of their letters
originally points to the first letter of claimed

explanation.surface: Welfare once claimed by needy people for bone and joint care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges AID THE POOR into ORTHOPAEDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthopaedic medicine corrects deformities of bones and muscles.

clue.text: Modest reduction of military unit

indicators.note: the military word is cut down to its standard short form

parts.note: a company is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: Cutting an army unit back is a humble move.
explanation.walkthrough: COY is the regular army abbreviation for company.
explanation.definitionFit: Coy means shy or bashful, reluctant to put oneself forward.

clue.text: Dairy product politician fed to pet

indicators.note: the politician goes inside the pet like food

parts.note: a cat is a typical pet
a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Cheese given to a politician's animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese.

clue.text: Of exceptional ability, but still not paid

definitions.meaning: unsettled, as a debt yet to be paid

explanation.surface: A brilliant worker who has still not received a salary.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses of the word: superb, and a bill remaining unsettled.

clue.text: Novel gains a lot, looking back wistfully

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book earns a great deal, with someone reminiscing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is a sentimental longing for the past.

clue.text: Like a whole range of climbers requisites

definitions.text: Like a whole range of climbers requisites

parts.words: Like a whole range of climbers requisites
parts.note: climbers need peaks to climb, and a whole range of them describes very hilly country

explanation.surface: Like a full catalogue of mountaineering kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' suggests a shop's product range of gear; it is a range of peaks, the thing climbers really require.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilly country with many peaks forming a range is described by this adjective.

clue.text: Firm still in the same premises?

explanation.surface: A company still at its old address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business, matching the premises; it is steadfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmoved means unaffected or resolute, and literally not relocated.

clue.text: Damage or impair, ignoring the odds

indicators.note: skipping the odd-placed letters of impair leaves the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: To harm or weaken, disregarding the betting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Or impair' looks like part of the definition; only impair is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar is to spoil or harm something.

clue.text: Italian physicist's study assimilated by girl out East

indicators.note: the study is absorbed into the girl's name
the East letter is taken out of the name

parts.note: Marie is a girl's name
to con is to study

explanation.surface: A scientist's research is absorbed by a girl abroad in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out East' reads like travel to Asia; it means the East letter is dropped from the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi was the Italian physicist who pioneered radio.

clue.text: Notes haphazardly made about Roman ruin

indicators.note: the rearranged made goes around the other piece
the letters of made are put together at random, in a new order
to ruin the word Roman is to wreck its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Messages jotted carelessly about a ruined Roman site.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures careless notes about a ruin; 'haphazardly' and 'ruin' are both anagram signals, one for each word, and 'about' wraps one result round the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda are written reminders, the plural of memorandum.

clue.text: In royal circles, a vessel with ample space

parts.note: O is circle-shaped, so two of them
MY is short for motor yacht

explanation.surface: Among high society, a boat offering plenty of room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal circles' looks like a single phrase about high society; it is R and OO.
explanation.definitionFit: Roomy means spacious.

clue.text: Parched Conservative goes in for bitter

indicators.note: the abbreviation enters the word for parched

parts.note: arid means parched, very dry

explanation.surface: A thirsty Tory orders a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bitter' looks like the British beer; it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrid taste or smell is sharp and harsh.

clue.text: . Live with duke in some luxury

parts.note: to live well is to live in comfort

explanation.surface: Living alongside a duke in comfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to reside somewhere.

clue.text: Green-eyed woman in English Intelligence

indicators.note: the woman sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: nous means common sense, intelligence
Vi is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A jealous female agent working in British intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is called the green-eyed monster, so green-eyed means jealous.

clue.text: So unhealthy, by the sound of it

indicators.note: the word for unhealthy is said aloud and spelt differently

parts.note: sick means unwell

explanation.surface: Feeling poorly, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: SIC is Latin for 'thus', used in [sic] to mark a quoted error.
explanation.definitionFit: Sic is the Latin for thus, marking text quoted exactly as found.

clue.text: Boxer, perhaps, knocked out? Damn it!

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
gone means unconscious, knocked out

explanation.surface: A fighter gets floored and someone swears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' suggests a fighter knocked out; it is the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggone is a mild American curse, a euphemism for damned.

clue.text: Sycophant's notes switched for the present

indicators.note: the musical notes A and D in the word trade places

parts.note: a toady is a sycophant

explanation.surface: A flatterer's messages are swapped for a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes switched' swaps A and D in TOADY; 'present' looks like a gift but is the current time.
explanation.definitionFit: Today means the present time, nowadays.

clue.text: Bird commander put out like cat

parts.note: CO is short for commanding officer

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An officer is as annoyed as a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' turns LIKE CAT into CKATIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatiel is a small crested Australian parrot.
